{{Short description|Characteristic subgroup in mathematical finite group theory}}
In [[Group theory#Finite group theory|finite group theory]], a branch of [[mathematics]], the '''Puig subgroup''', introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Puig|year=1976}}, is a [[characteristic subgroup]] of a [[p-group|''p''-group]] analogous to the [[Thompson subgroup]].

==Definition==

If ''H'' is a [[subgroup]] of a [[group (mathematics)|group]] ''G'', then ''L''<sub>''G''</sub>(''H'') is the subgroup of ''G'' generated by the [[abelian group|abelian]] subgroups normalized by ''H''.

The subgroups ''L<sub>n</sub>'' of ''G'' are defined recursively by
*''L''<sub>0</sub> is the [[trivial group|trivial]] subgroup
*''L''<sub>''n''+1</sub> = ''L''<sub>''G''</sub>(''L''<sub>''n''</sub>)
They have the property that
*''L''<sub>0</sub> ⊆ ''L''<sub>2</sub> ⊆ ''L''<sub>4</sub>... ⊆ ...''L''<sub>5</sub> ⊆ ''L''<sub>3</sub> ⊆ ''L''<sub>1</sub>

The '''Puig subgroup''' ''L''(''G'') is the [[intersection (set theory)|intersection]] of the subgroups ''L''<sub>''n''</sub> for ''n'' [[parity (mathematics)|odd]], and the subgroup ''L''<sub>*</sub>(''G'') is the [[union (set theory)|union]] of the subgroups ''L''<sub>''n''</sub> for ''n'' [[parity (mathematics)|even]].

==Properties==

Puig [[mathematical proof|proved]] that if ''G'' is a ([[solvable group|solvable]]) group of odd [[order (group theory)|order]], ''p'' is a [[prime number|prime]], and ''S'' is a [[Sylow subgroup|Sylow ''p''-subgroup]] of ''G'', and the ''{{prime|p}}''-core of ''G'' is trivial, then the [[center (group theory)|center]] ''Z''(''L''(''S'')) of the Puig subgroup of ''S'' is a [[normal subgroup]] of ''G''.
